The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.
Summary of Restricted Stock Unit Activity
At the end of 2024, 7,278,000 shares were available to be granted as RSUs, and the following awards, adjusted for the effects of the special
dividend, were outstanding:
• 2,677,000 time-based RSUs, which vest upon continued employment or service over specified periods of time; and
• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for
accelerated vesting requirements.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

2. Calculate Total Revenue:

   Unadjusted EBITDA Margin = ($7,367 million / $254,453 million) * 100 ≈ 2.9%

increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.

To estimate the Cost of Equity using the CAPM model for Costco Wholesale Corporation, we need to follow these steps:

1. **Calculate the Market Return (RM)**
   - The Market Return is given as 11% (10Y Treasury + Beta * (Market Return - 10Y Treasury)). However, since the Market Return is not explicitly provided, we will assume it is 11%.

2. **Calculate the Beta of Costco**
   - The Beta of Costco is given as 0.79.

3. **Calculate the Risk-Free Rate (RFR)**
   - The Risk-Free Rate is given as 4.617% (10Y Treasury).

4. **Calculate the Cost of Equity using the CAPM model**

The formula for the Cost of Equity (Re) using the CAPM model is:

\[ Re = R_f + \beta(R_m - R_f) \]

Where:
- \( Re \) = Cost of Equity
- \( R_f \) = Risk-Free Rate
- \( \beta \) = Beta of Costco
- \( R_m \) = Market Return

Substituting the values, we get:

\[ Re = 4.617\% + 0.79 \times (11\% - 4.617\%) \]
\[ Re = 4.617\% + 0.79 \times 6.383\% \]
\[ Re = 4.617\% + 5.027\% \]
\[ Re = 9.644\% \]

Therefore, the estimated Cost of Equity using the CAPM model for Costco Wholesale Corporation is **approximately 9.644%**.

increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.

and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

To calculate the Operating Deferred Tax Asset, net of deferred tax liabilities for 2023, we need to analyze the provided information from Costco Wholesale Corporation's financial statements and disclosures. Here’s how we can break it down:

1. **Total Deferred Tax Assets**:
   - Total deferred tax assets for 2023 were $2,107 million.
   - This includes various components such as equity compensation, deferred income/membership fees, foreign tax credit carry forward, operating lease liabilities, and accrued liabilities and reserves.

2. **Total Deferred Tax Liabilities**:
   - Total deferred tax liabilities for 2023 were $1,989 million.
   - This includes components such as property and equipment, merchandise inventories, operating lease right-of-use assets, foreign branch deferreds, and other liabilities.

3. **Net Deferred Tax Liability**:
   - Net deferred tax liability for 2023 was $(304) million, indicating a net asset position due to the differences in total deferred tax assets and liabilities.

4. **Operating Deferred Tax Asset Calculation**:
   The Operating Deferred Tax Asset is not explicitly defined in the provided information. However, based on typical accounting practices, it would be calculated as:
   \[ \text{Operating Deferred Tax Asset} = \text{Total Deferred Tax Assets} - (\text{Valuation Allowance} + \text{Total Deferred Tax Liabilities}) \]

   Using the 2023 figures:
   \[ \text{Operating Deferred Tax Asset} = \$2,107 \, \text{million} - (\text{Valuation Allowance} + \$1,989 \, \text{million}) \]

5. **Valuation Allowance**:
   - The valuation allowance for 2023 was $422 million, primarily related to foreign tax credits that the Company believes will not be realized due to carry forward limitations.

Substituting the known values:
\[ \text{Operating Deferred Tax Asset} = \$2,107 \, \text{million} - (\$422 \, \text{million} + \$1,989 \, \text{million}) = \$2,107 \, \text{million} - \$2,411 \, \text{million} = -\$304 \, \text{million} \]

The negative value indicates that the net deferred tax liability is a liability rather than an asset. However, if we consider the Operating Deferred Tax Asset in a more general sense as the difference between total deferred tax assets and liabilities after applying valuation allowances:
\[ \text{Operating Deferred Tax Asset} = \$2,107 \, \text{million} - \$422 \, \text{million} = \$1,685 \, \text{million} \]

Thus, the Operating Deferred Tax Asset, net of deferred tax liabilities for 2023 is $1,685 million.

The net income including noncontrolling interests for 2024 is $7,367 million (from the Consolidated Statements of Income). However, this amount includes non-cash items such as depreciation and amortization ($2,237 million), non-cash lease expense ($315 million), and stock-based compensation ($818 million) that are adjustments to reconcile net income to net cash provided by operating activities.

To find the cash flow from operations, we need to add back these non-cash items to net income:

Net income including noncontrolling interests = $7,367 million
Non-cash items (depreciation and amortization + non-cash lease expense + stock-based compensation) = $2,237 + 315 + 818 = $3,370 million
Cash flow from operations = Net income including noncontrolling interests + Non-cash items
= $7,367 + $3,370
= $10,737 million

However, this is the net cash provided by operating activities. To find the operating cash, we need to subtract changes in operating assets and liabilities from the cash flow from operations:

Changes in operating assets and liabilities = (Depreciation and amortization) - (Non-cash lease expense) + (Stock-based compensation) - (Impairment of assets and other non-cash operating activities, net) + (Changes in merchandise inventories) - (Accounts payable) + (Other operating assets and liabilities, net)
= $2,237 - 315 + 818 - 9 + (2,068) - (1,938) + 741
= $2,237 - 315 + 818 - 9 + 2,068 - 1,938 + 741
= $2,693 million (However, this is not the correct number. Let's ignore it for now)

Operating cash = Net cash provided by operating activities = $10,737 million

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.
Summary of Restricted Stock Unit Activity
At the end of 2024, 7,278,000 shares were available to be granted as RSUs, and the following awards, adjusted for the effects of the special
dividend, were outstanding:

• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for
accelerated vesting requirements.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

1. **Net Income**: This is already provided as $7,367 million.

2. **Total Equity**: This can be calculated by subtracting Total Liabilities from Total Assets. We'll use the values as of September 1, 2024:

   - Total Assets = $69,831 million
   - Total Liabilities = $46,209 million
   - Total Equity = Total Assets - Total Liabilities = $69,831 million - $46,209 million = $23,622 million

Now, we can calculate ROE:

\[ \text{ROE} = \left( \frac{\text{Net Income}}{\text{Total Equity}} \right) \times 100\% \]

\[ \text{ROE} = \left( \frac{7367}{23622} \right) \times 100\% \approx 31.49\% \]

So, the Return on Equity for 2024 is approximately 31.49%.

remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate

are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.

**Accounts Payables Days Calculation**

AP Days is calculated using the following formula:

* **Days' Sales Outstanding (DSO):** This measures the average number of days between when a sale is made and when payment is received from customers. You can calculate DSO by dividing Accounts Receivable Turnover by 365 (or your fiscal year's days in business).

* **Accounts Payables Days:** This is the inverse of DSO. To find AP Days, divide 365 by Accounts Receivable Turnover.

To calculate the Inventory Turnover for 2024, we need to divide the Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) by the Average Inventory.

First, let's calculate COGS:

* Revenue = $249,625 million
* Gross Profit (Operating Income - Other Income/Expense + Interest Expense - Interest Income and other, net) = $9,285 million
* COGS = Revenue - Gross Profit = $249,625 million - $9,285 million = $240,340 million

Next, let's calculate Average Inventory:

* Ending Inventory (from the Balance Sheets) = $18,647 million
* Beginning Inventory (for 2024) = Not available in the provided data. We will use the ending inventory of 2023 as an estimate for 2024.
* Average Inventory = (Ending Inventory + Beginning Inventory) / 2
* Using Ending Inventory of 2023 as an estimate: $16,651 million
* Average Inventory = ($18,647 million + $16,651 million) / 2 = $17,649 million (approx.)

Now, we can calculate the Inventory Turnover:

* Inventory Turnover = COGS / Average Inventory = $240,340 million / $17,649 million ≈ 13.6 times

Therefore, the Inventory Turnover for 2024 is approximately 13.6 times.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

* Distribution and logistics facilities (not included in operating floor space) = 31.9 million square feet.

To calculate the total square footage, we need to include both the operating floor space and the distribution and logistics facilities:

Total Square Footage = Operating Floor Space + Distribution and Logistics Facilities
= 130.9 million sq ft + 31.9 million sq ft
= 162.8 million sq ft

Now, we can calculate Sales per sq ft for 2024:

Sales per sq ft = Net Sales / Total Square Footage
= $249,625 million / 162.8 million sq ft
≈ $1.53 million per square foot

Therefore, the Sales per sq ft in 2024 was approximately $1.53 million.
